name: Magnesium

discovery.discoverer: Joseph Black (recognized as an element); isolated 1808 by Humphry Davy

occurrence: Abundant in seawater and minerals like dolomite and magnesite.
majorUses: Lightweight alloys for aircraft and car parts
biologicalRelevance: The central metal ion in chlorophyll, making it essential for photosynthesis, and a cofactor for hundreds of enzymes in the human body including ones used in muscle and nerve function.
notableCharacteristics: Burns with an extremely bright white flame hot enough to continue burning even underwater or in carbon dioxide.
whyHere: Losing both 3s electrons gives it a stable neon-like Mg²⁺ ion, and that same eagerness to donate electrons is what makes it burn so fiercely and vividly.
didYouKnow: Magnesium fires can't be put out with water or CO₂ extinguishers because burning magnesium reacts with both — sand or a Class D extinguisher is required instead.
genZNote: Burns so bright it doesn't care what you throw at it. Also quietly running your chlorophyll and half your enzymes.
